tasks.spec:
You are a Python worker on a personal executive-assistant repository at /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA. Your working directory is a scratch task directory; use it only for ./notes.md. Edit the repository at that absolute path.

OWNERSHIP. You own exactly ONE file: scripts/sources/intake.py. You are its only writer, deliberately, because four separate contracts converge on it. Do NOT edit anything under tests/ (two files there are hash-checked and are your specification), do NOT edit scripts/sources/linkedin_threads.py, hubspot_engagements.py, vault_wiring.py or money.py, do NOT edit state/plaid_items.json, do NOT edit anything under _config/, AGENTS.md or ROUTER.md, do NOT touch ~/.claude/skills/. Do not run git commit, git push or git add.

DO NOT RUN THE REAL PIPELINE. Do not execute scripts/sources/intake.py against live sources, do not call any API, and do not retrieve any real credential. The two frozen tests prove everything you need with stubs and fakes. If you are about to run something that would resolve a real credential value, stop.

CONTEXT. Three sibling modules were just built and all pass their own tests, but intake.py still calls the broken paths, so none of them is in service. Your job is to put them in service and to close two defects in code that landed earlier today.

SEVEN CHANGES.

(1) MOVE THE HEADER PARSE INSIDE THE PER-MESSAGE BOUNDARY. In gmail_items, the line building `h` from `full["payload"]["headers"]` currently sits AFTER the try/except that guards the API call. A header entry lacking "name" or "value" raises KeyError there, escapes gmail_items, and destroys the whole source. That is precisely the incident this function was rewritten to prevent, with the trigger moved from fetch to parse. Put the parse inside the same per-message boundary so a parse failure increments the same error counter and flows into the existing ceiling, note and RuntimeError machinery for free. Keep the retry semantics: a malformed payload is not transient and must not be retried.

(2) LOG THE UNREADABLE IDS TO STDERR. Today's entire investigation stalled on the question "which message?" because the id died with the exception. Write each failed message id to stderr, where run_daily.sh's tee lands it in state/runs/. Only FAILED ids may be logged; do not dump every id. Ids must NOT appear in the returned note or anywhere in the scan artifact: the scan carries counts for the brief's reader, the log carries ids for whoever reproduces it. Never log a subject, a sender or a body.

(3) NAME THE DOMINANT ERROR TYPE. The RuntimeError raised when errors exceed the ceiling currently carries both counts, which is the frozen invariant, but no indication of what went wrong. Add the dominant error type or status so the FAILED line in the scan says what kind of hole it was. Keep both counts exactly as they are; a frozen test asserts them.

(4) CLOSE THE BODY FENCE. Remove `hs_task_body` and `hs_note_body` from LABEL_KEYS. Nothing returns those fields today, so nothing leaks today; the moment any adapter requests them a task body containing a client or patient name renders straight into the scan. Neither the ingest redactor in this file nor scripts/gates/phi_scan.py detects a bare human name, and both say so in their own docstrings, so structural non-ingestion is the only control that works. Add a comment saying exactly that, so nobody helpfully adds them back.

(5) ADD THE ENVIRONMENT SEAM. Give `run_cli` an optional `env_extra` mapping merged into the child environment, defaulting to no extra environment, and let `cli_items` accept and forward it. This is the seam the credential wiring needs and it is the only signature change required.

(6) WIRE THE THREE MODULES INTO collect().
  - linkedin: keep invoking the skill's `chats --output json`, but format its stdout through `lines_from_payload` from scripts/sources/linkedin_threads.py instead of the generic labeler. That module is a pure formatter and returns the (items, truncated, note) 3-tuple this file already uses.
  - hubspot-tasks and hubspot-meetings: invoke the in-repo scripts/sources/hubspot_engagements.py with --type and --limit, instead of the shared skill's `engagements list`, which sends no properties param and is the reason both sources have failed every day. Format the records with that module's task_label and meeting_label, in the same way fathom_action is passed as a formatter today.
  - bills-due and money: resolve their environment at call time through scripts/sources/vault_wiring.py, using resolve_env with a caller named for the source, BILLCOM_ENV for bill.com, and plaid_env for the institutions listed in state/plaid_items.json. Pass the result as env_extra. A resolved value must never reach an argv this file constructs, a log line, or the scan.

(7) DELETE A FALSIFIED COMMENT. The comment above the openbrain sources claims the secret guard may resolve under a systemd timer. The 2026-08-07 08:50 run WAS the timer run and both openbrain sources failed in it, so that hypothesis is disproved, not open. Replace it with what is actually known: the launcher at ~/.claude/skills/open-brain/call.sh calls the retrieval tool and swallows its stderr, so a denied retrieval and an absent secret produce identical messages, and which one is happening is still unknown. Do not change the openbrain source's behavior; only the comment. While you are in the file, the module docstring's usage line says scripts/intake.py and the file lives at scripts/sources/intake.py; fix that too.

HOW TO VERIFY, from /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA, iterate until all pass:
  python3 tests/test_gmail_partial.py
  python3 tests/test_intake_wiring.py
  python3 /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-EA/16e106db-dbb9-44a1-936b-63218d06190f/scratchpad/check_integration.py

test_gmail_partial.py currently reports 6 failures, all in its cases 7 and 8, and cases 1 through 6 must STAY green. test_intake_wiring.py currently reports 12. Read both docstrings first; they carry the full contract and the reasoning behind each rule. The third command is what the run is graded on: it re-hashes both frozen tests, runs them, runs every other test file with no exemptions, and asserts you touched only intake.py.

STYLE. This file's comments name the incident each rule prevents rather than restating the code. Match that; it is the house style and it is why this repository is debuggable. No new dependencies. Keep the diff as small as each change allows.

OUTPUT. When all three commands pass, write ./notes.md naming each of the seven changes and how you verified it, the final output of all three commands, anything in the contract that turned out ambiguous, and any risk you are leaving behind.
tasks.verified: both frozen tests are byte-identical to the coordinator's versions and pass, every other test file passes with no exemptions, and the only modified file is scripts/sources/intake.py.
